answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, the binding constraint is delivery continuity, not price. memory_c2 supports that switching to the low-cost vendor historically cut unit cost with fast onboarding and accurate invoicing, and the low-cost quote alone meets the 18% mandate. That makes switch_primary_vendor the only candidate that satisfies the finance mandate within the 14-day window — but it concentrates supply, which is exactly the single-point-of-failure risk memory_c3 warned about. I verify c2 first to confirm the switch history holds before committing; if it does not, fallback is negotiate_terms with the incumbent. Dual-sourcing to mitigate risk is explicitly out of reach this cycle (one decision only), so the concentration risk is flagged rather than resolved.
